title: The Rake's Trick Against the Chaste Wife (മലയാളം)

full_text:
The Fourth Vizier related a comical history of how a virtuous woman defended her home with clever wit:

'In Cairo lived a lady of peerless beauty and sharp intellect named Fatima, whose husband was an honest merchant traveling in Syria. An unscrupulous young idler of the neighborhood resolved to compromise her reputation.

He hired an elderly woman to visit Fatima's house, carrying a little lapdog that had been fed meat rubbed with hot pepper, causing tears to stream from the creature’s eyes.

The old woman sat in the courtyard, stroked the weeping dog, and sighed with theatrical sorrow: "Alas, my daughter! Look upon this miserable little dog! She was once a beautiful maiden who refused the suit of a passionate lover; the lover cursed her, and she was transformed into this weeping beast!"

Fatima looked at the dog, and then at the old woman with a sharp, discerning smile. Perceiving the trick immediately, Fatima feigned profound terror:

"O mother! What a terrible warning! My husband is away, and I have five suitors who knock upon my door! If I refuse them, I shall be transformed into a dog! Bring the chief suitor to my house tonight, that I may save myself from enchantment!"

The overjoyed schemer arrived at her house that evening, dressed in his finest robes. Fatima welcomed him, served him spiced lentil soup, and invited him to inspect her husband’s private storeroom.

The moment he stepped inside, Fatima slammed the heavy cedar door, locked it with two iron bolts, and called out through the keyhole: "Stay there until morning, brave suitor! Tomorrow my husband and the Chief of Police will examine your transformation!"

At dawn, she delivered the shivering schemer to the city magistrate, earning the applause of the entire quarter for her courage and wit.'
moral: Purity of mind and witty composure outsmart the most elaborate traps of unscrupulous schemers. [ML]
